title: ML-Driven Log Analysis for Real-Time Cyber Threat Detection in Security Operation Centers
content: The escalating sophistication of cyber threats necessitates advanced threat detection in Security Operation Centers (SOCs). This study aims to enhance the capabilities of Wazuh, an open-source Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system, by addressing its primary limitation: high false positive rates in rule-based detection. We propose integrating machine learning (ML) to improve detection accuracy and operational efficiency. The approach involves training and evaluating ML models—Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, and Gaussian Naive Bayes—alongside clustering algorithms (DBSCAN, K-means, Isolation Forest) using 10-fold cross-validation. Results demonstrate that RF achieved the highest performance with an accuracy of 0.972, precision of 0.982, recall of 0.975, and F1-Score of 0.978, while DBSCAN excelled in clustering with a 91.06% accuracy and 0.0821 false positive rate. This integration significantly reduced false positives, enhancing alert management and enabling efficient real-time threat detection. The study contributes to cybersecurity by demonstrating that ML integration with Wazuh markedly improves threat detection, reduces operational overhead in SOCs, and establishes a more adaptive security framework.
